article_lead.description: constant mean and lag-dependent covariance in a time series, allowing one dependence pattern to be used across dates

new_bank_questions.title: Autocovariances of a stationary AR(1)
new_bank_questions.body: A stationary AR(1) has coefficient 0.4 and independent innovation variance 9. Find its variance γ(0), lag-one autocovariance γ(1), and lag-two autocorrelation ρ(2).
new_bank_questions.answer: The variance is 9/(1-0.4²)=75/7≈10.7143. Then γ(1)=0.4(75/7)=30/7≈4.2857, while ρ(2)=0.4²=0.16. These values are independent of the calendar origin under stationarity.

new_bank_questions.title: Stable moments, changing distributions
new_bank_questions.body: Independent even-time values equal -1 or 1 with equal chances. Independent odd-time values are uniform on [-√3,√3]. Is the combined series weakly stationary? Is it strictly stationary? Explain from means, variances, covariances and one-time distributions.
new_bank_questions.answer: Both marginals have mean 0 and variance 1; independence makes every nonzero-lag covariance 0. Hence the process is weakly stationary. The even-time law has two atoms but the odd-time law is continuous, so a one-step shift changes the marginal distribution and strict stationarity fails.
